en: As manufacturing activities expand, they will need to be supported by more robust knowledge- and skill-based economies, which will require higher investment in education to boost technical and vocational skills and training.
zh: 隨著製造業活動的擴張，需要更強大的以知識和技能為基礎的經濟的支援，這需要提高教育投資，提振技術和職業技能和培訓。

en: No country has ever undergone economic modernization without industry.
zh: 沒有一個國家可以在沒有工業的情況下實現經濟現代化。

en: But, more to the point, no functional industrial sector has ever emerged in the absence of strong, committed leadership.
zh: 但說得更透徹些，如果沒有強大堅定的領導力，就不會有能正常運轉的工業部門。

en: Consider Mauritius, which in the 1970s was a low-income mono-crop economy with a per capita GDP of just under $250.
zh: 以模里西斯為例，20世紀70年代，它還是一個低收入的單一作物經濟體，人均GDP只有250美元。

en: Today, Mauritius is an upper-middle-income country with a more diversified economy and a per capita GDP of around $9,600.
zh: 如今，它已是中上收入國家，經濟實現了多樣化，人均GDP高達9,600美元。

en: It is often cited as a model of economic success in Africa.
zh: 它經常被視為非洲經濟成功的榜樣。

en: How did this come about?
zh: 這一切是如何造就的？

en: As former Mauritian Prime Minister and President Anerood Jugnauth has put it, “There is no miracle.
zh: 模里西斯前首相兼總統賈格納特說 ： “ 沒有奇蹟。

en: It is due simply to hard work, discipline, and will.”
zh: 無非是努力工作、紀律和意志。

en: Leaders who want to develop a strong manufacturing base must have the political will to distribute resources fairly and pull the private sector along.
zh: ”想要發展強大製造業基礎的領導人必須具備政治意志公平分配資源並與私人部門攜手共進。

en: Mauritius experienced its fair share of challenges in moving from low-end manufacturing to technology-intensive goods and services.
zh: 模里西斯在從低端製造業向技術密集型商品和服務轉變時也遇到了各種挑戰。

en: But it now stands as an example of what committed leadership can accomplish.
zh: 但如今，它已成為堅定的領導力能夠取得什麼成就的範例。

en: Other African countries would do well to emulate it as they pursue their own economic transformations.
zh: 其他非洲國家在追求各自的經濟轉型時，若能效而仿之，必能取得成效。

en: All told, Africa is well placed to seize many of the opportunities that the global economy offers emerging markets.
zh: 總而言之，非洲大有希望能夠抓住全球經濟給新興市場帶來的諸多機會。

en: It already has the resources and the labor; now it needs committed leaders like Jugnauth who will implement the right policies.
zh: 它擁有資源和勞動力；現在，它需要賈格納特這樣的堅定的領導人來實施正確的政策。

en: Africa’s Alternative Path to Development
zh: 非洲的另一條發展路徑

en: WASHINGTON, DC – Recent projections indicate that several Sub-Saharan African countries will experience robust economic growth over the next five years.
zh: 發自華盛頓特區 — — 最近的幾項預測指出幾個撒哈拉以南非洲國家將在未來五年中實現強勁的經濟增長。

en: By 2023, around one-third of the region’s economies will have grown at an average annual rate of 5% or higher since 2000.
zh: 從2000年到2023年間，該地區約有1/3的經濟體將達到5％甚至更高的年均增長率。

en: And yet, as The Economist observed last year, Africa’s development model “puzzles economists.”
zh: 但正如《經濟學人》雜誌在去年觀察到的那樣，非洲的發展模式“讓經濟學家們感到困惑 ” 。

en: After all, only four of the continent’s high-growth countries are natural-resource dependent.
zh: 畢竟該大陸只有四個高增長國家是資源依賴型的。

en: Nor is overall performance due primarily to industrialization, as traditional development models would have predicted.
zh: 此外總體的發展也並不像傳統發展模式所預測的那樣主要由工業化所推動。

en: What, then, explains the strong economic performance?
zh: 那麼又該如何解讀這一強勁經濟表現呢？

en: New research by the Brookings Institution’s Africa Growth Initiative and the United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER) might hold the key to answering that question.
zh: 由布魯金斯學會的非洲增長倡議課題組和聯合國大學世界發展經濟研究所聯合進行的新研究可能擁有解答這個問題的鑰匙。

en: According to the forthcoming book Industries Without Smokestacks: Industrialization in Africa Reconsidered, there is evidence to suggest that Sub-Saharan Africa is undergoing a more profound structural transformation than we think.
zh: 根據即將出版的《無煙工業：對非洲工業化的重新思考》一書，有證據表明撒哈拉以南非洲正在經歷著比我們想象中更為深刻的結構性轉型。

en: Africa owes this structural transformation not to traditional industries, but to new developments in tradable services and agro-industries that resemble traditional industrialization.
zh: 非洲這種結構性轉型並非來自於傳統工業，而是類似傳統工業化程序的可貿易服務業和農業產業的新發展。

en: Aside from horticulture and agro-business, these new industries include information and communication technology-based services (ICT) and tourism.
zh: 除園藝和農產品業務外，這些新興產業還包括基於資訊和通訊技術的服務業和旅遊業。

en: This is a departure from the historical norm.
zh: 這就與歷史常態背道而馳。

en: Traditionally, as Harvard University economist Dani Rodrik points out, economies that have sustained robust growth rates without relying on natural-resource booms, “typically do so through export-oriented industrialization.”
zh: 傳統上，正如哈佛大學經濟學家丹尼·羅迪克指出的那樣，那些在不依賴高價自然資源的情況下保持強勁增長率的經濟體“通常透過以出口為導向的工業化來實現增長 ” 。

en: But in Africa, manufacturing as a share of total economic activity has stagnated at around 10%, with economic activity moving from agriculture to services.
zh: 但在非洲，製造業佔經濟活動總量的比例一直停留在10％左右，經濟活動也從農業直接跳到了服務業。

en: And because the rate of productivity growth in services is only about half that of manufacturing, the aggregate productivity gains needed for sustained growth have fallen relatively short.
zh: 由於服務業的生產率增長只有製造業的一半左右，因此實現持續增長所需的總體生產率增加值也相對較少。

en: This process of premature deindustrialization is not unique to Africa.
zh: 這種過早的去工業化程序可不是非洲獨有的。

en: But it is more consequential for the continent, given the scale of its development challenges.
zh: 但考慮到非洲所面臨的各項發展挑戰的規模，這一程序對這塊大陸的意義極為重大。

en: Owing to its young, rapidly growing labor force, Africa now needs to create more than 11 million jobs in the formal economy every year.
zh: 由於其勞動力大軍普遍年輕且增長迅速，非洲現在還需要每年在正規經濟中創造超過1100萬個就業崗位。

en: But as Nobel laureate economist Joseph E. Stiglitz has warned, Africa cannot replicate East Asia’s manufacturing-led model, so the question is whether it can leverage modern services to achieve economic development.
zh: 但正如諾貝爾經濟學獎得主約瑟夫·E·斯蒂格里茨（Joseph E. Stiglitz）所警告的那樣，非洲無法複製東亞那種製造業主導的模式，因此問題是它能否藉助現代服務來實現經濟發展。

en: According to Foresight Africa: Top Priorities for 2018, a Brookings Institution report previewing the results of Industries Without Smokestacks, services exports from Africa grew more than six times faster than merchandise exports between 1998 and 2015.
zh: 根據布魯金斯學會發布的《非洲前瞻：2018年的重點優先事項》報告 — — 該報告概述了《無煙工業》一書中的各項結論 — — 在1998到2015年間，非洲的服務出口增速比商品出口增速快了六倍以上。

en: In Kenya, Rwanda, Senegal, and South Africa, the ICT sector is flourishing.
zh: 在肯亞，盧安達，塞內加爾和南非，基於資訊和通訊技術的服務業都實現了蓬勃發展。

en: In Rwanda, tourism is now the single largest export activity, accounting for about 30% of total exports.
zh: 在盧安達，旅遊業已經成為規模最大的單一出口活動，佔到了該國出口總額的近30 ％ 。

en: Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, and Senegal are all integrated into global horticultural value chains, and Ethiopia has become a leading player in global flower exports.
zh: 衣索比亞，迦納，肯亞和塞內加爾都融入了全球園藝價值鏈，而衣索比亞也已晉身為全球花卉出口的主要參與者。

en: As these smokestack-less industries have grown, they have generated new patterns of structural change that are distinct from those of East Asia’s manufacturing-led transformation.
zh: 隨著這些無煙工業的發展，它們產生了與東亞製造業主導型轉型不同的新結構變化模式。

en: But, if properly stewarded, they could play the same role in Africa’s development as manufacturing did in East Asia.
zh: 如果進行適當的統籌管理，這些工業也可以在非洲的發展中扮演和東亞製造業一樣的角色。

en: First, manufacturing has higher productivity than agriculture, and it can absorb a large number of moderately skilled workers migrating out of the agriculture sector. Second, manufacturers benefit from technological transfers from abroad, so their productivity rises in line with global trends.
zh: 而製造業帶動的增長之所以能成為東亞地區有效的發展模式，主要有三大原因：首先，製造業的生產率高於農業，可以吸收大量從農業部門遷移出來的中等技術工人；其次，製造商受益於來自國外的技術轉讓，所以它們的生產率提升速率與全球趨勢同步；第三，東亞製造業以出口為導向，使得生產得以擴大。

en: According to John Page, one of the editors of Industries Without Smokestacks, Africa’s growing service sectors share these same characteristics.
zh: 正如《無煙工業》的編者之一約翰·佩奇（John Page）所說，非洲不斷增長的服務部門具備相同的特點。

en: In addition to being tradable, they have higher productivity and can absorb large numbers of moderately skilled workers.
zh: 除了可交易外，它們還具有較高的生產力，可以吸收大量中等技術工人。

en: And like manufacturing, they also benefit from technological change and economies of scale and agglomeration.
zh: 像製造業一樣，它們也受益於技術變革和經濟的規模集聚效應。

en: Moreover, Africa’s smokestack-less service sectors have the added advantage of being less vulnerable to automation.
zh: 此外，非洲這些無煙服務部門還具有不易受工業自動化影響的優勢。

en: Notwithstanding automation’s many benefits, it presents challenges for countries where the overriding priority is to create a sufficient number of formal-sector jobs.
zh: 儘管自動化有許多好處，但也為那些首要任務是創造足夠數量正規部門就業崗位的國家提出了挑戰。

en: While economists have been increasingly confident that Africa’s development model will be different from that of East Asia, they have been less certain about what shape it will take.
zh: 雖然經濟學家越來越確信非洲的發展模式會與東亞不同，但他們對這種模式的最終形式還不確定。

en: An industries-without-smokestacks model offers one possible answer.
zh: 為此一個無煙工業模式則提供了一個潛在的答案。

en: From a policy perspective, African leaders should explore more ways to support these industries’ growth, either through targeted reforms or by incorporating them into national industrialization strategies and broader development agendas.
zh: 從政策角度來看，非洲領導人應該透過有針對性的改革或將其納入國家工業化戰略以及更廣泛的發展議程來探索更多支援這些行業發展的方式。

en: The development of industries without smokestacks can occur alongside efforts to develop those with smokestacks, thus offering a multifaceted approach for Africa to achieve structural transformation.
zh: 無煙工業的發展可以與發展有煙工業的努力齊頭並進，從而為非洲實現結構轉型提供一個多方面多層次的路徑。

en: Banking on African Infrastructure
zh: 寄希望於非洲的基礎設施建設

en: JOHANNESBURG – As the US Federal Reserve embarks on the “great unwinding” of the stimulus program it began nearly a decade ago, emerging economies are growing anxious that a stronger dollar will adversely affect their ability to service dollar-denominated debt.
zh: 約翰內斯堡 — — 隨著美聯儲開始“大逆轉”近十年前開始的刺激計劃，新興經濟體越來越擔心美元走強會對其以美元計價債務的償付能力造成負面影響。

en: This is a particular concern for Africa, where, since the Seychelles issued its debut Eurobond in 2006, the total value of outstanding Eurobonds has grown to nearly $35 billion.
zh: 對非洲而言這種擔憂尤其嚴重，自塞席爾2006年發行首支歐元債以來，尚未償還的歐元債總值已經增長到近350億美元。

en: But if the Fed’s ongoing withdrawal of stimulus has frayed African nerves, it has also spurred recognition that there are smarter ways to finance development than borrowing in dollars.
zh: 但如果說美聯儲持續退出刺激計劃已經挑動了非洲國家的神經，同時也令人們意識到有比借美元債更加明智的發展融資方法。

en: Of the available options, one specific asset class stands out: infrastructure.
zh: 在現有方案中，有一種特定的資產類別脫穎而出：那就是基礎設施建設。

en: Africa, which by 2050 will be home to an estimated 2.6 billion people, is in dire need of funds to build and maintain roads, ports, power grids, and so on.
zh: 非洲預計到2050年人口將達26億左右，因此急需資金來修建和維護道路、港口、電網等基礎設施。

en: According to the World Bank, Africa must spend a staggering $93 billion annually to upgrade its current infrastructure; the vast majority of these funds – some 87% – are needed for improvements to basic services like energy, water, sanitation, and transportation.
zh: 據世界銀行統計，非洲必須每年花費驚人的930億美元用於升級其現有基礎設施；而這些資金中的絕大多數 — — 約佔87 % — —將用於改善能源、飲用水、衛生和交通運輸等基礎服務。

en: Yet, if the recent past is any guide, the capital needed will be difficult to secure.
zh: 但如果說過去有任何經驗可以借鑑，那就是籌措所需資金絕不是一項輕而易舉的任務。

en: Between 2004 and 2013, African states closed just 158 financing deals for infrastructure or industrial projects, valued at $59 billion – just 5% of the total needed.
zh: 在2004到2013年間，非洲國家僅實際完成了158項基礎設施或工業專案的融資交易，總值590億美元 — — 僅佔所需資金總額的5 % 。

en: Given this track record, how will Africa fund even a fraction of the World Bank’s projected requirements?
zh: 鑑於這樣的過往經歷，非洲能否籌措到世界銀行預測要求的哪怕一小部分資金都存在很大變數。

en: The obvious source is institutional and foreign investment.
zh: 最明顯的資金來源是機構和國外投資。

en: But, to date, many factors, including poor profit projections and political uncertainty, have limited such financing for infrastructure projects on the continent.
zh: 但到目前為止，許多因素，包括盈利預測不佳和政治不穩定，都對非洲大陸基礎設施專案的融資能力構成了嚴重的限制。

en: Investment in African infrastructure is perceived as simply being too risky.
zh: 對非洲基礎設施專案投資被視為高風險的選項。

en: Fortunately, with work, this perception can be overcome, as some investors – such as the African Development Bank, the Development Bank of Southern Africa, and the Trade & Development Bank – have already demonstrated.
zh: 幸運的是，就像一些投資者 — — 如非洲開發銀行、南部非洲開發銀行和貿易發展銀行 — — 已經證明的那樣，經過艱苦的努力，這種消極的看法可以被克服。

en: Companies from the private sector are also profitably financing projects on the continent.
zh: 來自私營部門的企業同樣可以在非洲大陸基礎設施專案融資當中有利可圖。

en: For example, Black Rhino, a fund set up by Blackstone, one of the world’s largest multinational private equity firms, focuses on the development and acquisition of energy projects, such as fuel storage, pipelines, and transmission networks.
zh: 例如，由黑石公司設立的黑犀牛基金是全世界規模最大的跨國私募股權公司之一，該基金專門從事燃料儲存、管道和輸送網路等能源專案的開發和採購。

en: But these are the exceptions, not the rule.
zh: 但這些皆屬例外，而非規則。

en: Fully funding Africa’s infrastructure shortfall will require attracting many more investors – and swiftly.
zh: 充分籌措資金解決非洲的基礎設施短缺問題需要迅速吸引更多的投資者。

en: To succeed, Africa must develop a more coherent and coordinated approach to courting capital, while at the same time working to mitigate investors’ risk exposure.
zh: 要想取得成功，非洲必須制定一種更為協調一致的方法來討好資本，並同時竭盡全力控制投資者的風險敞口。

en: Public-private sector collaborations are one possibility.
zh: 公共和私營部門合作提供了一種可能性。

en: For example, in the energy sector, independent power producers are working with governments to provide electricity to 620 million Africans living off the grid.
zh: 例如，在能源領域，獨立的電力生產企業正在與政府合作為6.2億尚未接入電網的非洲民眾提供電能。

en: Privately funded but government regulated, these producers operate through power purchase agreements, whereby public utilities and regulators agree to purchase electricity at a predetermined price.
zh: 這些電力生產企業由私人出資並接受政府監管，透過電力採購協議來完成運營，公共事業部門和監管機構在電力採購協議中同意以事先約定的價格採購電力供應。

en: There are approximately 130 such producers in Sub-Saharan Africa, valued at more than $8 billion.
zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲地區約有130家這樣的電力生產企業，總值超過80億美元。

en: In South Africa alone, 47 projects are underway, accounting for 7,000 megawatts of additional power production.
zh: 僅南非一地就在開展47個相關專案，總共可以達到7000兆瓦的新增電力產能。

en: Similar private-public partnerships are emerging in other sectors, too, such as transportation.
zh: 交通運輸等其他部門也正在出現類似的公私合作關係。

en: Among the most promising are toll roads built with private money, a model that began in South Africa.
zh: 其中最有前景的當屬最早出現在南非的由私人投資興建的收費公路。

en: Not only are these projects, which are slowly appearing elsewhere on the continent, more profitable than most financial market investments; they are also literally paving the way for future growth.
zh: 這些在非洲大陸其他地方逐漸出現的專案不僅比多數金融市場投資更有利可圖；而且正在事實上為未來的經濟增長鋪平道路。

en: Clearly, Africa needs more of these ventures to overcome its infrastructure challenges.
zh: 顯而易見，非洲需要更多這樣的合資公司才能迎接基礎設施所帶來的挑戰。

en: That is why I, along with other African business leaders and policymakers, have called on Africa’s institutional investors to commit 5% of their funds to local infrastructure.
zh: 因此我和非洲商業領袖及決策者共同呼籲非洲機構投資者將5%的資金用於投資當地的基礎設施。

en: We believe that with the right incentives, infrastructure can be an innovative and attractive asset class for those with long-term liabilities.
zh: 我們相信只要激勵措施得當，基礎設施對那些擁有長期負債的機構而言完全可以成為創新且有吸引力的資產類別。

en: One sector that could lead the way on this commitment is the continent’s pension funds, which, together, possess a balance sheet of about $3 trillion.
zh: 能夠領導這一目標的部門之一是非洲大陸的養老基金，該部門合計擁有約3萬億美元的資產負債表。

en: The 5% Agenda campaign, launched in New York last month, underscores the belief that only a collaborative public-private approach can redress Africa’s infrastructure shortfall.
zh: 上個月在紐約啟動的5%議程行動強調了這樣一種理念，即僅有公私合作方式能夠改變非洲的基礎設施短缺。

en: For years, a lack of bankable projects deterred international financing.
zh: 多年以來，缺乏銀行貸款專案阻礙了國際融資。

en: But in 2012, the African Union adopted the Program for Infrastructure Development in Africa, which kick-started more than 400 energy, transportation, water, and communications projects.
zh: 但2012年，非洲聯盟透過了非洲基礎設施開發計劃，啟動了超過400個能源、交通運輸、水資源和通訊專案。

en: It was a solid start – one that the 5% Agenda seeks to build upon.
zh: 這是一個相當不錯的開始 — — 也是5%議程行動賴以存在的基礎。

en: But some key reforms will be needed.
zh: 但必須進行某些關鍵領域的改革。

en: A high priority of the 5% Agenda is to assist in updating the national and regional regulatory frameworks that guide institutional investment in Africa.
zh: 5%議程行動的重要目標是協助升級國家和地區監管框架，從而引導非洲的機構投資。

en: Similarly, new financial products must be developed to give asset owners the ability to allocate capital directly to infrastructure projects.
zh: 同樣，必須開發新的金融產品，以便資產所有者能夠將資金直接劃撥給基礎設施專案。

en: Unlocking new pools of capital will help create jobs, encourage regional integration, and ensure that Africa has the facilities to accommodate the needs of future generations.
zh: 解鎖新的資金池將有助於創造就業機會、鼓勵區域一體化及確保非洲擁有能滿足子孫後代需求的基礎設施專案。

en: But all of this depends on persuading investors to put their money into African projects.
zh: 但所有這些都取決於能否說服投資者將資金投入非洲建設專案。

en: As business leaders and policymakers, we must ensure that the conditions for profitability and social impact are not mutually exclusive.
zh: 身為商界領袖和決策者，我們必須確保賺取利潤和社會影響的條件能夠相互融合。

en: When development goals and profits align, everyone wins.
zh: 如果發展目標能夠和利潤保持一致，那麼所有人都是贏家。

en: Freeing Africa’s Internet
zh: 解放非洲的網際網路

en: WASHINGTON, DC – Much to the dismay of the government in Addis Ababa, “Zone 9” has become a household name in Ethiopia.
zh: 華盛頓—讓亞的斯亞貝巴政府大吃一驚的是 ， “ 第九區 ” （ Zone 9）成了衣索比亞一個家喻戶曉的名字。

en: Since 2012, this small group of journalists-turned-online activists has used social media to campaign for political freedoms and civil liberties in their country.
zh: 2012年以來，這個線上記者活躍分子團體利用社交媒體要求國家實現政治自由和公民自由。

en: The group’s success – measured, for example, by the flood of likes and comments on its Facebook page – has come in spite of government efforts to silence the writers, including the arrest of six members in 2014 on trumped-up terrorism charges.
zh: 它的成功 — — 比如可以用其Facebook頁面上的點贊和評論數量衡量 — — 是在政府試圖讓寫手噤聲的情況下取得的，包括2014年六名成員因為子虛烏有的恐怖主義指控而被逮捕。

en: Ethiopia’s government is not alone in seeking to consolidate political power by restricting what citizens say online.
zh: 衣索比亞政府不是唯一一個試圖透過限制公民的網路言論來鞏固政治權力的政府。

en: Across Africa, governments are enacting legislation to restrict Internet access and outlaw criticism of elected officials.
zh: 放眼非洲，許多政府都實施了限制網際網路接入、將對當選官員的批評入罪的法律。

en: Digital campaigners face myriad censorship tactics, including “Border Gateway Protocol” attacks, “HTTP throttling,” and “deep packet inspections.”
zh: 數字活動家面對各種審查技術，如“邊界閘道器協議”攻擊 、 “ HTTP限流”和“深層封包檢測”等。

en: The irony, of course, is that censorship rarely quiets the disaffected.
zh: 當然，諷刺的是審查很少能夠讓不滿噤聲。

en: Rather than quelling dissent, government intervention only inspires more people to take their grievances to WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter, and other social media platforms, where Africans are increasingly challenging corrupt governments, exposing rigged elections, and demanding to be heard.
zh: 政府幹預非但不能鎮壓異見，反而刺激了更多的人在WhatApp、Facebook、Twitter和其他社交媒體平臺上宣洩不滿，非洲人透過這些渠道對日益挑戰腐敗的政府、曝光被操縱的選舉，並要求自己的聲音被聽到。

en: At the moment, however, few of Africa’s leaders are listening.
zh: 但此時此刻，很少有非洲領導人在聆聽。

en: Leaders in nine of the 18 African countries that held elections in 2016 placed some level of restriction on the Internet to limit dissent.
zh: 在2016年舉行了選舉的18個非洲國家中，有九個國家的領導人實施了某種程度的網際網路限制以遏制異見。

en: Four days prior to Uganda’s presidential vote in February, President Yoweri Museveni cut access to mobile payment services and social media sites.
zh: 2月份烏干達總統選舉投票前四天，總統穆塞韋尼切斷了移動支付服務和社交媒體網站。

en: In August and September, Gabon’s president, Ali Bongo, seeking to project an atmosphere of calm to the international community, shut down Internet access overnight.
zh: 8月和9月，加彭總統班戈意欲在國際社會面前營造平靜的氛圍，關閉了夜間網際網路接入。

en: Then in December, officials in Democratic Republic of the Congo ordered an Internet shutdown the day before President Joseph Kabila was scheduled to leave office, thereby quashing online dissent when he refused to step down.
zh: 12月，民主剛果官員下令在總統卡比拉卸任前一天關閉網際網路，以壓制他拒絕下臺所引發的網上異見。

en: Internet blackouts like these violate people’s human rights and undermine democratic processes.
zh: 這類斷網行為違反了人權，也破壞了民主程序。

en: Last year, the United Nations Human Rights Council approved a resolution affirming that, “rights that people have offline must also be protected online, in particular freedom of expression.”
zh: 去年，聯合國人權委員會透過了一項決議，重申“人們線上下的權利，線上上也必須得到保護，特別是言論自由。 ”

en: Most African governments try to justify Internet embargoes by arguing that the restrictions are necessary to ensure public safety and security.
zh: 大部分非洲政府用辯稱斷網是為了確保公共安全和安保而不得已而為之。

en: Museveni, for example, claimed that blocking Internet access was the only way to protect visiting heads of state during his swearing-in ceremony.
zh: 比如，穆塞韋尼宣稱切斷網際網路接入是在其就職典禮上保護來訪的各國首腦的唯一辦法。

en: But he presented no evidence linking social media accessibility and security in Uganda, or anywhere else.
zh: 但他沒有拿出任何證據證明社交媒體接入和烏干達或其他任何國家的安全有什麼聯絡。

en: According to Access Now, an international advocacy group for digital rights, people typically feel less secure without the Internet, because they cannot access information or connect with friends and family in times of uncertainty.
zh: 據推動數字權利的國際團體“馬上連通 ” （ Access Now）組織的資料，斷網通常讓人感到更不安全，因為人們無法在不確定時獲得資訊或與親朋取得聯絡。

en: With several key African elections coming up, Internet shutdowns are again on the horizon.
zh: 隨著多個非洲國家重要選舉的臨近，斷網也再次走進人們的視野。

en: In Zimbabwe, where President Robert Mugabe, who is 93, is expected to run for his eighth term in mid-2018, a government-led crackdown appears inevitable.
zh: 在辛巴威，93歲的總統穆加貝預計將履任其第八個總統任期（從2018年年中開始 ） ， 政府主導的鎮壓行動看來已是勢在必行。

en: For decades, Mugabe has relied on intimidation and violence to stifle political dissent.
zh: 幾十年來，穆加貝依靠恐嚇和暴力扼殺政治異見。

en: It is not surprising, then, that he has already begun taking a hostile approach to online activism.
zh: 因此，毫不奇怪，他早已對線上活動持敵對態度。

en: Last year, his government shut down the Internet in the middle of political protests, and vowed to arrest anyone caught generating or sharing “abusive or subversive material on social media.”
zh: 去年，他的政府在政治示威期間關閉了網際網路，並宣稱要逮捕所有制造或分享“社交媒體上的誹謗或顛覆性材料”的人。

en: But citizens are not helpless.
zh: 但公民並非無望。

en: While governments issue orders to cut off Internet access, only telecommunications companies have the ability to hit the “kill switch.”
zh: 政府固然可以下令斷網，但只有通訊公司有能力按下“死亡開關 ” 。

en: That is why Africa’s bloggers and online activists must work more closely with investors and shareholders of communications firms to convince them to stand up for democracy and human rights by resisting illiberal government directives.
zh: 因此，非洲部落格寫手和線上活動家們必須更加緊密地與通訊企業的投資者和股東合作，說服他們力挺民主和人權，拒絕反自由的政府指令。

en: Moreover, civil-society groups, the African Union, and the UN should do more to condemn national legislation that aims to normalize restrictive Internet policies.
zh: 此外，公民社會團體、非洲聯盟和聯合國應該加大力度譴責旨在將限制網際網路的政策常規化的立法。

en: Just as it launched a model law on access to information in 2013, the African Union should provide new guidance to states on how to safeguard the right to assemble and express views online.
zh: 2013年，非盟釋出了資訊接觸示範法，如今，它應該為各國提供新的指引，教它們如何捍衛線上收集和表達觀點的權利。

en: Finally, new continent-wide measures are needed to ensure that Africans’ online rights are recognized and respected by their governments.
zh: 最後，需要新的洲級措施確保非洲線上權利得到政府和承認和尊重。

en: Although the UN Human Rights Council’s resolution to protect online freedoms is not binding, it offers a starting point for ensuring that governments allow citizens to use the Internet as a tool for maximizing political participation.
zh: 儘管保護線上自由的聯合國人權委員會決議不具有約束力，但它為確保政府允許公民將網際網路用作政治參與最大化的工具提供了一個起點。

en: Such interventions are needed now more than ever.
zh: 這些干預比以往任何時候都更加需要。

en: The Kenyan, Zimbabwean, and Ethiopian legislatures are currently considering laws that would permit significantly greater government control over Internet access.
zh: 肯亞、辛巴威和衣索比亞立法機關正在考慮顯著擴大政府網際網路接入管制權的立法。

en: Last year, Tanzania adopted legislation that has already been used to charge individuals with crimes who have criticized President John Magufuli on social media.
zh: 去年，坦尚尼亞實施了一項立法，被用來對在社交媒體上批評總統馬古富力的個人提起刑事指控。

en: Whether governments bar citizens from gathering in public, signing petitions, or accessing the Internet and posting on social media makes no difference.
zh: 不管政府是禁止公民公開集會、簽署請願書，還是禁止公民接入網際網路並在社交媒體上發帖，並沒有什麼區別。

en: All such measures are designed to strip citizens of their rights.
zh: 所有這些措施都是為了剝奪公民的權利。

en: The battle for freedom, as Zone 9 has shown, is no less real when the public square is the digital domain.
zh: 第九區表明，為了自由的鬥爭在數字領域和在公共廣場上一樣真實。

en: Capturing Africa’s High Returns
zh: 抓住非洲的高回報機遇

en: WASHINGTON, DC – Since 2000, at least half of the world’s fastest-growing economies have been in Africa.
zh: 華盛頓 — — 自2000年來，至少半數世界增長最快的經濟體來自非洲地區。

en: And by 2030, Africa will be home to 1.7 billion people, whose combined consumer and business spending will total $6.7 trillion.
zh: 而截至2030年，非洲將擁有17億人口，其消費和商業支出的總額將高達6.7萬億美元。

en: Seven years ago, the Harvard Business Review pointed out that Africa is also home to many of the world’s biggest opportunities.
zh: 七年前，哈佛商業評論就曾指出非洲是全世界最大的機遇所在地。

en: And yet, despite its tremendous business potential, Africa has not risen to the top of Western business leaders’ agendas.
zh: 但儘管商業潛力巨大，非洲卻並沒有被西方商業領袖作為議程的重中之重。

en: In fact, between 2014 and 2016, US exports to Africa fell by almost half, from $38 billion to $22 billion.
zh: 事實上，從2014到2016年間，美國對非洲出口驟降近半，從美元380億下降到美元220億。

en: And while the United Kingdom’s investments on the continent more than doubled between 2005 and 2014, reaching £42.5 billion ($57.6 billion), only 2.5% of its total exports are to Africa.
zh: 而儘管英國對非洲大陸的投資在2005到2014年間增長超過一倍，達到425億英鎊（合576億美元 ） ， 但針對非洲的出口總額僅佔2.5 % 。

en: Western countries are quickly losing ground to China, which increased its exports to Africa more than sevenfold – to $103 billion – from 2005 to 2015.
zh: 西方國家面對中國的挑戰正迅速喪失優勢，從2005到2015年間，中國對非洲的出口增長了七倍以上 — — 高達1，030億美元。

en: If Western businesses hope to keep up, they will need to tap into the African countries and sectors with the highest potential for growth.
zh: 如果西方企業想要跟上中國的腳步，他們就必須充分利用非洲增長潛力最大的國家和部門。

en: By 2030, more than half of Africa’s population will reside in seven countries: Nigeria, Ethiopia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Egypt, Tanzania, Kenya, and South Africa.
zh: 到2030年，非洲超過一半的人口將居住在七個國家：包括奈及利亞、衣索比亞、剛果民主共和國、埃及、坦尚尼亞、肯亞和南非。

en: But, more important, 43% of Africans will belong to the middle or upper classes, up from 39.6% in 2013, implying considerably higher demand for goods and services.
zh: 但更重要的是，43%的非洲人將上升至中上階層， 而該資料在2013年僅為39.6 % ， 而這意味著對商品和服務的需求將大幅增加。

en: By 2030, household consumption is expected to reach $2.5 trillion, up from $1.1 trillion in 2015.
zh: 截止2030年，家庭消費預計將達到2.5萬億美元，而2015年的家庭消費總額僅有1.1萬億。

en: Nearly half of that $2.5 trillion will be spent in three countries: Nigeria (20%), Egypt (17%), and South Africa (11%).
zh: 其中三個國家將佔到這2.5萬億美元消費總額的近半數：他們是奈及利亞（20 % ） 、埃及（17 % ） 和南非（11 % ） 。

en: But there will also be lucrative opportunities in Algeria, Angola, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Sudan, and Tunisia.
zh: 但阿爾及利亞、安哥拉、衣索比亞、迦納、肯亞、摩洛哥、蘇丹和突尼西亞均存在能提供豐厚回報的機遇。

en: Any one of these countries would be a good bet for companies seeking to enter new markets.
zh: 上述國家中的任何一個都可以提供開拓新市場的良好機會。

en: By 2030, the sectors generating the most value in Africa will be food and beverages ($740 billion), education and transportation ($397 billion), and housing ($390 billion).
zh: 截至2030年，食品飲料（7，400億美元 ） 、 教育交通（3，970億美元）和住房（3，900億美元）將成為非洲創造最大價值的行業。

en: But there will also be strong growth in consumer goods ($370 billion), hospitality and recreation ($260 billion), health care ($175 billion), financial services ($85 billion), and telecommunications ($65 billion).
zh: 但消費品（3，700億美元 ） 、 酒店和娛樂（2，600億美元 ） 、 醫療保健（1，750億美元 ） 、 金融服務（850億美元）和電信服務（650億美元）同樣將會增長強勁。

en: Of course, much of this growth will depend on the African Union properly implementing its new Continental Free Trade Area, which would create a single market for goods and services, offering corporations many points of entry.
zh: 當然，增長最終能否實現將取決於非洲聯盟能否成功推行其新大陸自由貿易區。 這項政策將創造一個統一的商品和服務市場，為企業提供不止一個切入點。

en: Moreover, the CFTA will increase the need for connectivity, so there will be new opportunities to invest in infrastructure and sectors ranging from transportation and energy to information and communications technology (ICT) and water supplies.
zh: 不僅如此，新大陸自由貿易區將提升互聯互通的必要性，從而在基礎設施和從交通、能源、資訊及通訊技術（ICT）到供水等各行各業創造新的投資機遇。

en: For its part, the African Development Bank can help investors find promising projects through its Program for Infrastructure Development in Africa.
zh: 在這方面，非洲開發銀行可以透過其非洲基礎設施發展計劃幫助投資者找到前景廣闊的專案。

en: Another major growth area between now and 2030 will be in African business-to-business spending, which will reach $4.2 trillion, up from $1.6 trillion in 2015.
zh: 非洲企業對企業支出將成為從現在起到2030年另外一個主要增長領域，該支出總額將達4.2萬億美元，而2015年僅有美元1.6萬億。

en: Here, the largest sectors will be agriculture and agricultural processing ($915 billion), manufacturing ($666 billion), and construction, utilities, and transportation ($784 billion), followed by wholesale and retail ($665 billion), resources ($357 billion), banking and insurance ($249 billion), and telecommunications and ICT ($79.5 billion).
zh: 其中最主要的部門將包括農業和農產品加工（9，150億美元 ） 、 製造（6，660億美元 ） 、 建築、公共設施及交通（7，840億美元 ） ， 其次還有批發和零售（6，650億美元 ） 、 資源（3，570億美元 ） 、 銀行和保險（2，490億美元）以及電信和資訊及通訊技術（795億美元 ） 。

en: The expected growth in agriculture and agricultural processing reflects the fact that food and beverages will constitute the largest share of total household spending.
zh: 農業及農產品加工業的預期增長反映了食品飲料將佔據非洲家庭開支最主要份額的現實。

en: Moreover, 60% of the world’s unused arable land is in Africa, which still contributes a meager share of worldwide agricultural exports.
zh: 不僅如此，地球60%的閒置土地均位於非洲，即便如此，非洲仍然能為世界農業出口盡一份微薄之力。

en: That means there is a lot of room for growth.
zh: 這意味著非洲擁有巨大的增長潛力。

en: And, because severe hunger still affects many African countries, investors can even contribute to the public good by investing in fertilizers, machinery, water and irrigation systems, and other areas of the agriculture sector.
zh: 而且，由於嚴重饑荒仍影響許多非洲國家，投資者甚至可以透過投資肥料、機械、供水及灌溉系統以及農業部門的其他領域推動實現公共利益。

en: As of 2012, the African countries with the highest agricultural value-added in terms of annual growth included Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Mali, Mozambique, Rwanda, and Tanzania.
zh: 截止2012年，農業增加值年增長率最高的非洲國家包括布吉納法索、衣索比亞、奈及利亞、馬裡、莫三比克、盧安達和坦尚尼亞。

en: In addition, Angola, Morocco, and South Africa now all have sizable markets, and have committed to expanding their agricultural sectors.
zh: 不僅如此，安哥拉、摩洛哥和南非現在都擁有規模龐大的市場，並致力於擴大其農業部門的實力。

en: According to the Harvard Business Review, Africa also has the potential to become “the world’s next great manufacturing center.”
zh: 據哈佛商業評論報道，非洲同樣具備成為“世界下一個大型製造中心的潛力 ” 。

en: China is expected to lose from 85-100 million low-cost, labor-intensive manufacturing jobs by 2030, and Africa stands to capture many of them.
zh: 截至2030年，中國預期將喪失8，500萬到1億個低成本、勞動密集型的就業崗位，而非洲將成為其中許多崗位的承接地。

en: This helps to explain why manufacturing will be the second-largest sector in terms of business-to-business spending.
zh: 這有助於說明企業對企業支出的第二大領域為什麼是製造業。

en: Another reason is that many of the manufacturing opportunities in Africa happen to be in globally competitive sectors such as automobiles and transport equipment, refined petroleum, computers, and office and industrial machinery.
zh: 另一個原因是非洲許多製造業機遇恰恰來自於像汽車及運輸裝置、石油精煉、計算機、辦公及工業機械等全球性競爭領域。

en: South Africa, Egypt, and Nigeria are already becoming promising places to invest in these areas.
zh: 南非、埃及和奈及利亞已經成為投資上述領域的新興之地。

en: And investors will also be able to find high returns and favorable business environments in Ethiopia, Morocco, and Rwanda.
zh: 投資者也能在衣索比亞、摩洛哥和盧安達找到高回報和有利的商業環境。

en: Africa is the world’s last frontier market, and Western businesses need to start taking advantage of its tremendous potential, as Chinese firms already are.
zh: 非洲是世界最後一塊前沿市場，西方企業需要效仿中國，開始發掘其所擁有的巨大潛力。

en: Doing business in Africa will also create sustainable jobs and advance the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals to eliminate poverty and hunger.
zh: 在非洲開展業務還能在創造可持續就業機會的同時推動完成聯合國消滅飢餓和貧困的可持續發展目標任務。

en: And that, too, will be good for the bottom line.
zh: 而這歸根結底也是件好事。

en: As the Business and Sustainable Development Commission has shown, pursuing the SDGs “could raise trillions in new market opportunities in ways that extend prosperity to all.”
zh: 正如商業及可持續發展委員會所表明的那樣，實現可持續發展目標“能夠以一種令所有人都興旺發達的方式開拓價值數萬億美元的全新市場機遇。 ”

en: Strengthening African Science
zh: 加強非洲的科學

en: URBANA, ILLINOIS – In late March, Africa’s leading scientists, innovators, and policymakers met in Kigali, Rwanda, to brainstorm solutions to an increasingly pressing problem: the low quality of science on the continent.
zh: 烏爾班納，伊利諾伊州—3月底，非洲著名科學家、創新者和決策者齊聚盧安達基加利，為一個日益緊迫的問題展開頭腦風暴尋找解決方案：非洲低劣的科學質量。

en: Any good leader knows that scientific discovery and innovation fuels progress, facilitates development, and can help tackle issues like food insecurity, water shortages, and climate change.
zh: 優秀領導人都知道，科學發現和創新驅動進步、促進發展，還有助於解決糧食不安全、水短缺和氣候變化等問題。

en: And yet most African governments are failing to fund research and development adequately in their countries.
zh: 但大部分非洲國家政府都沒有為國內研究和開發提供足夠的資金。

en: According to the UNESCO Institute for Statistics, countries in Sub-Saharan Africa spend, on average, just 0.5% of GDP on research and development.
zh: 據聯合國教科文組織統計局，撒哈拉以南非洲各國平均研發支出僅佔GDP的0.5 % 。

en: In the West, the share is closer to 3%.
zh: 在西方，這一比例接近3 % 。

en: This disparity underscores the development challenges that Africans face.
zh: 這一差距構成了非洲所面臨的發展挑戰。

en: Africa is home to 15% of the world’s population and 5% of its GDP, but accounts for a paltry 1.3% of total research spending.
zh: 非洲人口佔世界的15 % ， GDP佔5 % ， 但研究總支出只佔1.3 % 。

en: Moreover, African inventors hold just 0.1% of the world’s patents, meaning that even when money is spent on science, innovation, and research, the findings rarely translate into solutions for the continent’s most immediate challenges.
zh: 此外，非洲創新者只擁有世界專利的0.1 % ， 這意味著即使把錢用在了科學、創新和研究上，成果也很少能轉化為解決非洲最緊迫挑戰的方案。

en: To be sure, these trends are not universal; some African governments are investing heavily in science-led innovation.
zh: 平心而論，這些趨勢並非放之非洲而皆準；一些非洲政府中金投資於科學驅動的創新。

en: In South Africa, for example, authorities have pledged to double R&D spending by 2020 – to 1.5% of GDP.
zh: 比如，在南非，當局承諾到2020年將研發支出提高一倍，至GDP的1.5 % 。

en: This follows a 2016 commitment by African heads of state to increase science and technology budgets to at least 1% of GDP by 2025.
zh: 在此之前，2016年非洲各國首腦承諾到2025年至少將科學技術預算提高到GDP的1 % 。

en: A handful of countries – including Kenya, Rwanda, and Senegal – are working hard to reach this funding threshold.
zh: 少數國家 — — 包括肯亞、盧安達和塞內加爾 — — 正在努力達到這一撥款閾值。

en: Africa also benefits from generous research-related aid and international support.
zh: 非洲也從慷慨的研究相關援助和國際支援中獲益。

en: One of the top donors, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, has invested more than $450 million in African science initiatives over the last decade.
zh: 貢獻最大的捐助者之一比爾和梅琳達·蓋茨基金會在過去十年中位非洲科學專案投入了4.5億多美元。

en: Projects include a $306 million program to boost crop yields and a $62.5 million grant to improve health outcomes.
zh: 這些專案包括一個3.06億美元的作物增產計劃和一筆6,250萬美元的健康改善資金。

en: These and other funding streams have helped African researchers develop drought-resistant crops, produce vaccines for infectious diseases like Ebola, and expand opportunities for science and technology education.
zh: 這些和其他資金流幫助非洲研究者開發了抗旱作物，為埃博拉等傳染病生產疫苗，增加了科學和技術教育的機會。

en: Unfortunately, many African governments lack the resources to fund programs that could build on these gains.
zh: 不幸的是，許多非洲政府缺少為可以在這些收益的基礎上更進一步的專案提供資金的資源。

en: Simply put, a new, more collaborative approach to African science is urgently needed.
zh: 簡言之，非洲科學急需更有合作精神的新方案。

en: Africa’s leaders have pooled their science resources before.
zh: 非洲領導人曾經集中過他們的科學資源。

en: In 2003, the African Union and the New Partnership for Africa’s Development began implementing a continent-wide strategy “to develop and use science and technology for the socioeconomic transformation of the continent and its integration into the world economy.”
zh: 2003年，非盟和非洲開發新合作計劃（New Partnership for Africa’s Development）開始實施一項洲際戰略 “開發和運用科學和技術推動非洲社會經濟轉型、促使其融入世界經濟。

en: It was an ambitious goal that yielded early results.
zh: ”這是一個宏偉的目標，並已經產生了早期結果。

en: Between 2005 and 2014, continent-wide spending on R&D increased, while research output more than doubled in many countries.
zh: 2005—2014年，非洲研發支出實現增長，許多國家的研究產出不止翻番。

en: Since then, however, progress has stalled.
zh: 但此後進展陷入了停滯。

en: The recent meeting in Rwanda, hosted by President Paul Kagame and organized by the Next Einstein Forum, was designed to help get the agenda back on track.
zh: 最新的盧安達會議由下一個愛因斯坦論壇（Next Einstein Forum）組織，總統卡加姆主持，旨在幫助該日程重回正軌。

en: But summits are only part of the solution; governments must also commit to improving research quality, and they can start by focusing attention on three key areas.
zh: 但峰會只是解決方案的一部分；政府還必須致力於改善研究質量，它們可以從關注三個關鍵領域開始。

en: First, Africa’s leaders must engage with CEOs, philanthropists, and donors who understand the long-term value of investing in science.
zh: 首先，非洲領導人必須與瞭解科學投資的長期價值的CEO、慈善家和捐贈者合作。

en: Innovation is expensive, and seed money will be needed to help strengthen the continent’s scientific capacity.
zh: 創新是昂貴的，需要種子基金幫助強化非洲的科學能力。

en: Second, African universities and institutions should align their research agendas with national and regional goals.
zh: 其次，非洲大學和機構應該理順研究日程與國家和地區目標的關係。

en: For example, given that one of Africa’s most pressing challenges is feeding its growing population, schools specializing in agricultural research should ensure that their work contributes to solutions.
zh: 比如，非洲最緊迫的挑戰是養活日益增長的人口，專注於農業研究的院校應該確保它們的工作有助於這一目標。

en: Last but not least, countries should encourage entrepreneurship within research organizations.
zh: 第三，各國應該鼓勵研究組織內部的企業家精神。

en: One way to do this is by establishing commercialization offices, which could help scientists bring their research to market.
zh: 一個辦法是建立商業化辦公室，商業化辦公室有助於科學家的研究面向市場。

en: Scientists everywhere need help navigating bureaucracy when turning an idea into a commercial venture, and this process is particularly challenging in a region where R&D pipelines are in their infancy.
zh: 各國科學家在將概念轉化為商業專案時，都需要幫助應付官僚主義，而這一過程在研發渠道尚處在襁褓階段的地區尤其具有挑戰性。

en: Boosting Africa’s scientific capabilities will require the continent’s leaders to do more than ask tough questions at summits; they must also allocate more funding and forge new partnerships.
zh: 提高非洲的科學實力需要非洲領導人不僅僅要在峰會上提出尖銳的問題；他們還必須配置更多的資金，構建新的合作關係。

en: To overcome Africa’s human development challenges, African governments must invest in the people who can overcome them.
zh: 要克服非洲的人類發展挑戰，非洲政府必須投資於能夠克服這些挑戰的人。

en: The High Cost of Food Monopolies in Africa
zh: 非洲糧食壟斷的高昂代價

en: LAGOS – In May, global food prices increased 1.2%, reaching their highest level since October 2017.
zh: 拉各斯—5月，全球糧食價格上漲1.2 % ， 達到了2017年10月以來的最高水平。

en: This upward trajectory is having a disproportionate impact in Africa, where the share of household income spent on food is also rising.
zh: 這波漲勢正在給非洲造成非常大的影響，家庭用於糧食的支出比例也節節攀升。

en: To ensure food security, governments must work quickly to reverse these trends, and one place to start is by policing the producers who are feeding the frenzy.
zh: 為了確保糧食安全，政府必須迅速行動起來扭轉這些趨勢，一個起點是整頓囤積居奇的生產商。

en: According to data compiled by the World Economic Forum, four of the world’s top five countries in terms of food expenditure are in Africa.
zh: 據世界經濟論壇收集的資料，全世界糧食支出最高的五個國家有四個在非洲。

en: Nigeria leads the list, with a staggering 56.4% of household income in 2015 spent on food, followed by Kenya (46.7%), Cameroon (45.6%), and Algeria (42.5%).
zh: 奈及利亞高居榜首，2015年56.4%的家庭收入用在了食品上，其次是肯亞（46.7 % ） 、喀麥隆（45.6 % ） 和阿爾及利亞（42.5 % ） 。

en: By comparison, consumers in the United States spend the least globally (6.4%), far less than people in emerging economies like Brazil (16%) and India (30%).
zh: 相比而言，美國消費者的支出為全球最低（6.4 % ） ，遠低於巴西 (16 % ) 和印度 (30 % ) 等新興經濟體。

en: One reason for the distortion is the price of food relative to income.
zh: 如此扭曲的一個原因是相對於收入的糧食價格。

en: As Africa urbanizes, people are buying more imported semi- or fully processed foods, which cost more than locally produced foods.
zh: 隨著非洲日漸城市化，人們開始購買更多進口半加工或全加工食品，這些食品比本地生產的食品更貴。

en: And in most countries, wages have not kept pace with inflation.
zh: 而在大部分國家，工資趕不上通貨膨脹。

en: But the primary cause is poor public policy: African governments have failed to curb the power of agribusinesses and large food producers, a lack of oversight that has made local agriculture less competitive.
zh: 但主要原因是拙劣的公共政策：非洲政府沒有遏制農商企業和大型食品製造商的權力，缺乏監督導致本地農業競爭力低下。

en: In turn, prices for most commodities have risen.
zh: 反過來，大部分大宗商品價格節節上漲。

en: The absence of antitrust laws, combined with weak consumer protection, means that in many countries, only two or three major companies control markets for items like salt, sugar, flour, milk, oil, and tea .
zh: 反壟斷法的缺位，加上消費者保護不足，導致在許多國家兩三家大公司控制了鹽、糖、麵粉、奶、油和茶等東西的市場。

en: The impact is most pronounced in African cities, where prices for white rice, frozen chicken, bread, butter, eggs, and even carbonated soft drinks are at least 24% higher than in other cities around the world.
zh: 非洲城市所受到的影響最為突出，白米、冷凍雞肉、麵包、黃油、雞蛋甚至碳酸飲料的價格要比世界其他城市至少高出24 % 。

en: These prices hit consumers both directly and indirectly (owing to pass-through of higher input costs by food conglomerates and service providers).
zh: 這些價格直接間接地影響著消費者（透過推高食品生產集團和服務提供商的投入品成本傳導 ） 。

en: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has long argued that food security and fair pricing depends on markets that are free from monopolistic tendencies.
zh: 聯合國糧農組織一直強調，糧食安全和公平定價取決於市場不能走向壟斷。

en: The OECD concurs, and has frequently called on authorities to address “anti-competitive mergers, abuse of dominance, cartels and price fixing, vertical restraints, and exclusive practices” in the food sector.
zh: 經合組織國家頻繁要求當局解決糧食行業的“反競爭兼併、濫用主導地位、卡特爾和固定價格、縱向約束以及排斥行為”問題。

en: And yet, in many African countries, this advice has rarely been heeded.
zh: 但是，在許多非洲國家，這一建議很少有人會聽。

en: To be sure, this is not a new problem.
zh: 平心而論，這並不是什麼新問題。

en: Between 1997 and 2004, for example, the FAO counted 122 allegations of “anti-competitive practices” in 23 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa. Violations included a “vertical monopoly” in the Malawi sugar sector, price fixing in Kenya’s fertilizer industry, and a “buyer cartel” in the Zimbabwean cotton industry.
zh: 比如，1997—2004年間，糧農組織在23個撒哈拉以南非洲國家發起了122宗“反競爭行為”指控。 違法行為包括馬拉維糖業的“縱向壟斷 ” 、 肯亞化肥業的價格固定，以及辛巴威棉花業的“買家卡特爾 ” 。

en: And, despite the considerable attention such cases have received, the underlying problems persist.
zh: 而儘管這些案件引起了廣泛關注，其根本問題頑固依舊。

en: According to the World Bank, more than 70% of African countries rank in the bottom half globally for efforts to protect “market-based competition.”
zh: 據世界銀行，超過70%的非洲國家在全球保護“基於市場的競爭”行為排行榜上位於後半部分。

en: While 27 African countries and five regional blocs do have antitrust laws on the books, enforcement is rare.
zh: 27個非洲國家和5個地區已經有了成文的反壟斷法，但幾乎沒有執法可言。

en: The remaining countries have no regulations at all and have made little progress in drafting them.
zh: 其他國家根本沒有反壟斷規則，連起草工作都鮮有國家在推進。

en: There is one notable exception: South Africa.
zh: 南非是一個顯著的例外。

en: Since 1998, the country’s Competition Act has prohibited any company controlling at least 45% of the market from excluding other firms or seeking to exercise control over pricing.
zh: 1998年以來，南非競爭法禁止任何公司透過排斥其他企業或尋求操縱價格控制45%或以上的市場份額。

en: Violators face penalties of up to 10% of their earnings, and during the last two decades, some of the biggest companies in the country – including Tiger Brands, Pioneer Foods, and Sime Darby – have been penalized.
zh: 違反者面臨高達收益的10%的罰款，在過去二十年中，南非的一些公司巨頭，如Tiger Brands、Pioneer Foods和森達美（Sime Darby ） ， 都被罰過款。

en: As Tembinkosi Bonakele, head of South Africa’s Competition Commission, noted last year, the government is “determined to root out exploitation of consumers by cartels,” especially in the food industry.
zh: 南非競爭委員會主席特姆賓柯西·博納科勒（Tembinkosi Bonakele）在去年指出，政府“決心杜絕卡特爾剝削消費者的現象 ， ” 特別是在糧食行業。

en: Other countries should follow South Africa’s lead.
zh: 其他國家應該效仿南非的榜樣。

en: Companies and special-interest groups will always seek to benefit from the absence of regulation.
zh: 公司和特殊利益集團永遠不會停止尋求鑽監管的空子獲益。

en: The need for reform is greatest in countries like Nigeria and Ghana, where food expenditures are high and food-industry pressure is most pronounced.
zh: 奈及利亞和迦納等國家最需要改革，在這些國家，糧食支出比例畸高，糧食安全壓力最大。

en: Fortunately, there is growing recognition of the need to address these challenges.
zh: 幸運的是，越來越多的人開始認識到必須解決這些挑戰。

en: Babatunde Irukera, Director General of the Consumer Protection Council in Nigeria, recently asserted that, “In a large vibrant and loyal market such as Nigeria, the absence of broad competition regulation is tragic.
zh: 奈及利亞消費者保護委員會總幹事巴巴吞德·伊魯克拉（Babatunde Irukera）最近表示 ， “ 在奈及利亞這樣的生機勃勃又忠誠的大市場，廣泛的競爭監管缺位實屬悲劇。

en: Unregulated markets in competition context constitute the otherwise ‘legitimate’ vehicle for both financial and social extortion.”
zh: 競爭環境中的不受監管的市場淪為金融和社會敲詐的‘合法’外衣。 ”

en: Reducing the prices of staple food by even a modest 10% (far below the average premium cartels around the world charge) by tackling anticompetitive behavior in these sectors, or by reforming regulations that shield them from competition, could lift 270,000 people in Kenya, 200,000 in South Africa, and 20,000 in Zambia out of poverty.
zh: 透過處置這些行業的反競爭行為，或透過改革阻止競爭的監管，從而降低主糧價格，哪怕只是區區10 % （ 遠低於全球卡特爾所要求的的平均溢價 ） ， 都能讓270,000肯亞人、200,000南非人、20,000辛巴威人擺脫貧困。

en: Such a policy would save households in these countries over $700 million (2015 US dollars) a year, with poor households gaining disproportionately more than rich ones.
zh: 這一政策將為這些國家的家庭每年節省超過7億美元（2015年美元 ） ， 貧窮家庭所得到的好處要遠大於富裕家庭。

en: Ultimately, it is the responsibility of political leaders to protect consumers from collusion and price-fixing.
zh: 說到底，保護消費者免受勾結和價格固定影響是政治領導人的責任。

en: There is no question that Africa’s businesses need space to innovate and grow, but their success should never come at the cost of someone else’s next meal.
zh: 毫無疑問，非週期也需要透過創新實現增長的空間，但它們的成功決不能以某些人的下一頓飯為代價。

en: The Cancer Threat to Africa’s Future
zh: 非洲未來的癌症威脅

en: CHICAGO – One of the most pressing public-health challenges in Africa today is also one of the least reported: cancer, a leading cause of death worldwide.
zh: 芝加哥 — — 當今非洲最緊迫的公共衛生挑戰之一也是報道最少的：那就是癌症，世界各地最主要的死亡原因。

en: Every year, some 650,000 Africans are diagnosed with cancer, and more than a half-million die from the disease.
zh: 每年都有約650,000非洲人被確診患有癌症，並有超過50萬人因這種疾病而死亡。

en: Within the next five years, there could be more than one million cancer deaths annually in Africa, a surge in mortality that would make cancer one of the continent’s top killers.
zh: 未來五年內，非洲可能每年都有超過100萬人因癌症死亡，死亡率激增將使癌症成為非洲大陸最主要的致死疾病。

en: Throughout Sub-Saharan Africa, tremendous progress has been made in combating deadly infectious diseases.
zh: 在整個撒哈拉以南非洲地區，人們在打擊致命傳染病方面取得了重大的進步。

en: In recent decades, international and local cooperation have reduced Africa’s malaria deaths by 60% , pushed polio to the brink of eradication, and extended the lives of millions of Africans infected with HIV/AIDS.
zh: 近幾十年來，國際和地方合作已成功將非洲的瘧疾死亡人數降低了60 % 、 幾乎完全根除了小兒麻痺症，並延長了數以百萬計感染艾滋病毒/艾滋病的非洲人的生命。

en: Unfortunately, similar gains have not been made in the fight against non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including cancer.
zh: 不幸的是，在抗擊包括癌症在內的非傳染性疾病（NCDs）的過程中並沒有取得類似的進步。

en: Today, cancer kills more people in developing countries than AIDS, malaria, and tuberculosis combined.
zh: 今天，癌症在發展中國家致死的人口數量比艾滋病、瘧疾和肺結核加起來還要多。

en: But, with Africa receiving only 5% of global funding for cancer prevention and control, the disease is outpacing efforts to contain it.
zh: 但由於非洲僅獲得全球癌症預防和控制資金的5 % ， 遏制癌症的努力根本趕不上這種疾病的蔓延速度。

en: Just as the world united to help Africa beat infectious disease outbreaks, a similar collaborative approach is needed to halt the cancer crisis.
zh: 正如全世界聯合起來幫助非洲遏制傳染病爆發一樣，必須採取類似的手段來遏制這場癌症危機。

en: Surviving cancer requires many things, but timely access to specialists, laboratories, and second opinions are among the most basic.
zh: 癌症患者生存需要許多東西，但及時得到專家、實驗室和補充診療意見卻是最基本的。

en: Yet, in much of Africa, a lack of affordable medications, and a dearth of trained doctors and nurses, means that patients rarely receive the care they need.
zh: 但在非洲絕大部分地區，廉價的藥品、訓練有素的醫生和護士都極為短缺，這意味著患者很少能夠得到他們所需要的護理服務。

en: On average, African countries have fewer than one trained pathologist for every million people, meaning that most diagnoses come too late for treatment.
zh: 平均而言，非洲國家每百萬人口僅有不到一位訓練有素的病理學家，這意味著絕大多數人無法在癌症尚可治療期間獲得準確的診斷服務。

en: According to University of Chicago oncologist Olufunmilayo Olopade, a diagnosis of cancer in Africa is “nearly always fatal.”
zh: 按照芝加哥大學腫瘤學家Olufunmilayo Olopade的說法，非洲的癌症診斷“幾乎總是致命的 ” 。

en: Building health-care systems that are capable of managing infectious diseases, while also providing quality cancer care, requires a significant investment in time, money, and expertise.
zh: 建設能夠管理傳染性疾病、同時也能提供優質癌症護理服務的醫療保健系統需要在時間、金錢和專業知識方面進行巨大的投入。

en: Fortunately, Africa already has a head start.
zh: 幸運的是，非洲已經有了一個不錯的開頭。

en: Past initiatives – like the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, the US President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, and the World Bank’s East Africa Public Health Laboratory Networking Project – have greatly expanded the continent’s medical infrastructure.
zh: 過去的各項計劃 — — 如防治艾滋病、結核病和瘧疾全球基金、美國總統艾滋病緊急救濟計劃以及世界銀行東非公共醫療實驗室聯網計劃 — — 都已經極大拓展了非洲大陸的醫療基礎設施建設。

en: National efforts are also strengthening pharmaceutical supply chains, improving medical training, and increasing the quality of diagnostic networks.
zh: 非洲各國也在強化藥品供應鏈、改善醫療培訓並提升診斷網路的服務質量。

en: Still, Africans cannot face down this threat alone.
zh: 但非洲人仍然無法獨自面對這樣的威脅。

en: That is why the American Society for Clinical Pathology, where I work, is cooperating with other global health-care innovators to attack the region’s growing cancer crisis.
zh: 我所在機構美國臨床病理學會因此正在與其他全球醫療保健創新機構合作來遏制非洲地區癌症危機的蔓延勢頭。

en: We have teamed up with the American Cancer Society (ACS) and the pharmaceutical company Novartis to support cancer treatment and testing efforts in four countries: Ethiopia, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda.
zh: 我們已經與美國癌症協會（ACS）和諾華製藥展開合作，支援衣索比亞、盧安達、坦尚尼亞和烏干達等四國的癌症治療和檢測工作。

en: Together, we have brought immunohistochemistry, a key diagnostic tool, to seven regional laboratories, an effort we hope lead to more timely cancer diagnoses and greatly improve the quality of care.
zh: 我們已經一起將重要診斷工具“免疫組織化學染色法”帶到了7家地區實驗室，我們希望這樣可以更及時地作出癌症診斷並極大地改善護理質量。

en: To complement these technical efforts, the ACS is also training African health-care professionals how to carry out biopsies and deliver chemotherapy.
zh: 美國癌症協會還培訓非洲專業醫療人士如何進行活檢和化療，以補充上面所提到的技術性工作。

en: That initiative, funded by Novartis, is viewed as a pilot program that could expand to other regional countries.
zh: 這項由諾華資助的計劃被視為有可能向其他區域國家拓展的一項試點工作。

en: Finally, our organizations are advocating for enhanced cancer-treatment guidelines in national health-care planning efforts, protocols that we believe are essential to improving health outcomes.
zh: 最後，我所在機構正在倡導在國家醫療保健計劃工作中強化癌症治療的指導原則，我們認為這樣的條款規定能在改善醫療效果的過程中發揮至關重要的作用。

en: These initiatives are in conjunction with other undertakings, such as a joint ACS-Clinton Health Access Initiative program to broaden access to cancer medications.
zh: 上述條款與美國癌症協會-克林頓聯合健康計劃相結合，以擴大癌症治療藥物的普及度。

en: When the world took notice that infectious diseases like HIV/AIDS, polio, and malaria were ravaging Africa, action plans were drawn up and solutions were delivered.
zh: 當世界各國意識到艾滋病毒/艾滋病、小兒麻痺症和瘧疾等傳染性疾病在非洲肆虐，我們制定了行動計劃並積極付諸行動。

en: Today, a similar global effort is needed to ensure that every African with a cancer diagnosis can get the treatment they need.
zh: 今天，人們必須推進類似的全球工作，以確保每位被確診患有癌症的非洲人都能得到所需的治療服務。

en: Now, as then, success depends on coordination among African governments, health-service providers, drug makers, and non-governmental organizations.
zh: 現在和當時一樣，非洲政府、醫療服務提供商、製藥企業和非政府組織之間的合作決定了抗擊癌症能否取得成功。

en: There is no place on Earth that is immune from the dread of a cancer diagnosis; wherever the news is delivered, it is often devastating to recipients and their families.
zh: 地球上沒有哪個地方不對癌症診斷充滿恐懼；無論哪裡的患者得到訊息，對接受者及其家庭來說會產生災難性的後果。

en: But geography should never be the deciding factor in patients’ fight to survive the disease.
zh: 但地理位置永遠不應成為患者與癌症鬥爭的決定性因素。

en: Cancer has been Africa’s silent killer for far too long, and the global health community must no longer remain quiet in the face of this crisis.
zh: 癌症作為非洲沉默的殺手已經太久，而面對這場危機全球醫療界絕對不應再保持沉默。

en: Investing in Africa’s Educators
zh: 投資非洲的教育者

en: JOHANNESBURG – Improving education is a slow, arduous, long-term undertaking everywhere, and nowhere more so than in Africa, where tight economic constraints often prevent sustained investment in human capital.
zh: 約翰內斯堡—教育的改善是一個緩慢、艱苦、長期的過程，不論在哪裡都是如此，非洲更加如此。 經濟的吃緊然常常讓非洲無法持續投資於人力資本。

en: Those who work in the education sector on the continent have to seek solutions that are faster, cheaper, and can be scaled up.
zh: 非洲教育工作者必須找到更迅速、更廉價並且能夠推廣的解決方案。

en: Too often, though, expedient approaches prove shortsighted, and fail to engage local leaders who hold the keys to economic and social progress.
zh: 但是，權宜之計往往相當短視，無法讓座位經濟和社會進步的關鍵的地方領導者參與進來。

en: Too often, grassroots-level voices, reflecting firsthand experience addressing their communities’ problems, are ignored.
zh: 草根的聲音往往被忽視，而這些聲音又往往反映瞭解決發聲者所在社群的問題的第一手經驗。

en: When global leaders gather in Hamburg this week for the G20 summit, the new G20-Africa Partnership will take center stage.
zh: 本週，全球領導人將在漢堡舉行G20峰會，新的G20-非洲合作計劃將成為中心議題。

en: But those committed to helping Africa should focus squarely on the nuts and bolts of aid and development – and that means investing in local leadership.
zh: 但致力於幫助非洲的仁人志士應該將注意力對準援助與發展的要害 — — 而這意味著投資於地方領導力。

en: Sadly, the best-funded aid organizations in Africa are often run by Westerners, or by Africans who have extensive ties to the West.
zh: 悲哀的是，在非洲，資金充裕的援助組織往往由西方人負責管理，而不是由於西方關係密切的非洲人負責管理。

en: I recently spoke to several entrepreneurs who shared anecdotal evidence that organizations in Africa with a Western co-founder raise more than twice the funds of African-run organizations.
zh: 我最近從幾位企業家那裡獲知，有西方聯合創始人的非洲組織，能夠籌集到比由非洲人負責管理的組織多一倍的資金。

en: This financial prejudice is visible elsewhere, too, and it is perpetuating the dearth of local talent.
zh: 這一金融偏見隨處可見，導致地方人才永久性流失。

en: The pro-Western bias should worry everyone working to build better communities for our children.
zh: 對於任何致力於為兒童創造更好的社群的人來說，親西方的偏見值得憂慮。

en: When it comes to addressing social issues – whether it’s educational inequity, poverty, or discrimination – the most committed advocates are those who have first-hand knowledge of the problem they seek to solve.
zh: 在解決社會問題時 — — 不管是教育不平等、貧困還是歧視 — — 最著力的支持者總是那些對需要解決的問題具備第一手經驗的人。

en: Personal experience is the best way to create agents for change, because it underpins people’s long-term, personal investment in dismantling systems that exacerbate inequity and injustice.
zh: 個人經驗是最好的變化催化劑，因為它能夠在一個不平等和不公平不斷加劇的分崩離析的系統中支援人們的長期個人投資。

en: What would it look like if the leaders overhauling such systems were cultivated from the very communities that needed them most?
zh: 如果修補這些系統的領導者正是從最需要他們的社群中長大，情況會怎麼樣？

en: Some organizations are answering that question already.
zh: 一些組織已經開始回答這個問題了。

en: More than 12,000 people have applied to join Teach For Nigeria, a national organization that recruits, trains, and places young teachers in high-need schools.
zh: 12,000多人申請加入奈及利亞教育計劃（Teach For Nigeria ） 。 這是一個全國性組織，招募和培訓年輕教師，然後分配到急需他們的學校。

en: The program, designed as a fellowship, will choose fewer than 60 of Nigeria’s brightest university graduates and professionals, not only to develop excellent classroom teachers, but also to empower the next generation of social entrepreneurs committed to tackling inequity and deeply connected to local efforts already underway in communities across their country.
zh: 該計劃是一個獎學金專案，它將遴選不多於60名奈及利亞最優秀的大學畢業生和專業人士，不但要培養優秀的講課教師，也要給致力於解決不平等性，並與已經在全國社群蓬勃開展的地方措施關係密切的下一代社會創業家賦權。

en: After their two-year teaching commitment, which begins in September, these up-and-coming leaders will join a worldwide movement of over 55,000 people who have completed the fellowship in over 40 countries, including the 30 fellows already hard at work next door at Teach for Ghana.
zh: 在經過從9月份開始為期兩年的教學承諾後，這些成長起來的領導者將加入一場包括55,000多人的全球性運動，這些人來自40多個國家，都完成了類似的獎學金專案，包括迦納教育計劃（Teach for Ghana）所培養的、現在已經投入到艱苦工作中去的30位獎學金獲得者。

en: We call this powerful grouping of change-agents “collective leadership,” and we believe it is the only way to ensure positive, lasting change.
zh: 我們將這個強大的變化推動者群體成為“集體領導者 ” ， 我們相信這是確保持續的積極變化的唯一方法。

en: Inadequate investment in locally led initiatives is one of the two ways in which we fail to ensure that those who are most affected by inequity have pathways to address it.
zh: 地方領導的計劃的投資不足是我們無法保證受不平等性影響最大的群體能夠找到辦法糾正這個問題的兩大原因之一。

en: The second is the failure to invest in children.
zh: 另一個原因是我們沒有投資於兒童。

en: In Uganda, 70% of children do not complete primary school.
zh: 在烏干達，70%的兒童無法完成小學學業。

en: Basic education is the foundation for our lifelong ability to analyze information, present ideas and opinions, and challenge the world around us.
zh: 基礎教育是我們分析資訊、形成思想和觀點、挑戰周邊世界的終身能力的基礎。

en: And yet, in too many African communities, we are failing to invest in laying those foundations.
zh: 但是，在太多非洲社群，我們並沒有致力於投資這些基礎。

en: Across the continent, educational attainment is sharply stratified: while 82% of children from the wealthiest families complete primary school, only 28% of children from the poorest families do.
zh: 在整個非洲，入學率分層明顯：82% 的富裕家庭兒童可以完成小學教育，而最貧窮家庭兒童的這一比例只有28 % 。

en: If the future of the continent is to be shaped by, or with, those who have most acutely experienced its challenges, programs like Teach for Nigeria and Teach for Ghana are essential.
zh: 如果非洲的未來將由被這一挑戰傷害最深的人所決定或影響，那麼奈及利亞教育計劃和迦納教育計劃等專案就是至關重要的。

en: Imagine what could be accomplished if efforts to place local recruits in low-income schools were expanded.
zh: 想象一下，如果能夠將本地招募的教師分配到低收入學校的措施得到推廣，會發生生麼。

en: Imagine how many opportunities to address the challenges facing children and families could be created, potentially reaching hundreds of thousands of children who are also inspired and encouraged to think critically and resolve the problems affecting the world around them.
zh: 想象一下，有多少解決兒童和家庭所面臨的挑戰的機會會被創造出來，並有可能覆蓋數十萬有志向並被孤立進行批判性思考和解決周邊世界的問題的兒童。

en: Some argue that education is meaningless if graduates cannot find work; in fact, job creation in Africa will be a major topic of discussion at the G20 summit.
zh: 有人指出，如果畢業了找不到工作，那麼教育就毫無意義；事實上，非洲就業創造也將是G20峰會的一個重大議題。

en: But while investment in business development and job creation is crucial for economic vitality and growth, it won’t happen without an educated workforce.
zh: 但是，儘管企業發展和就業創造投資對於經濟活力和增長至關重要，但如果沒有受過教育的勞動力，一切都是空談。

en: A robust job market presupposes a sufficient number of skilled workers to fill available jobs.
zh: 強健的就業市場首先需要有足夠多的高技能工人填補現成的工作崗位。

en: But in Sub-Saharan Africa, only 58% of children complete primary school.
zh: 但在撒哈拉以南非洲，只有58% 的兒童能夠從小學畢業。

en: This is why, when G20 leaders discuss new economic development strategies for Africa, they should focus on investment in education.
zh: 正因如此，G20領導人在討論新的非洲經濟發展戰略時，應該關注教育投資。

en: But, more important, they should seek to ensure that resources make it to those who rely on local leadership and innovation.
zh: 但更重要的是，他們應該確保資源用於依靠地方領導力和創新的人。

en: Sustainable Development Goal 4 – to ensure equitable and inclusive education for all by 2030 – is attainable, but only if solutions come from the ground up, which means from the Africans most committed to them.
zh: 可持續發展目標4 — — 到2030年確保平等包容的教育 — — 是可以實現的，但解決方案必須要“接地氣 ” ， 即要接入最渴望教育的非洲人民這個“地氣 ” 。

en: Empowering the Other Half of Africa’s Economy
zh: 賦權非洲經濟的另一半

en: JOHANNESBURG – Julius Nyerere, the founding president of Tanzania, once said that “unity” will not make Africa rich, but “it can make it difficult for Africa and the African peoples to be disregarded and humiliated.”
zh: 約翰內斯堡—坦尚尼亞建國總統朱利烏斯·尼雷爾曾說 ， “ 聯合”無法讓非洲變富，但“可以讓非洲和非洲人民不再那麼容易被輕視、被屈辱。

en: But, two decades later, Africa remains divided along a key fault line: gender.
zh: ”但是，二十年過去了，仍然有一條斷層線將非洲一分為二，那就是性別。

en: To realize Nyerere’s vision of a strong, dignified continent, Africa needs a new era of liberation, one that is fueled by the economic empowerment of the continent’s women.
zh: 要想實現尼雷爾的讓非洲成為一個強大的、有尊嚴的大洲的願景，非洲需要一個自由的新時代，為非洲婦女經濟賦權能夠為這個時代增添動力。

en: Although projections by the consultancy McKinsey anticipate that by 2040, Africa will have the world’s largest labor force, with more than 1.1 billion people of working age, more than 60% of Africa’s current population still survive on less than $2 a day.
zh: 麥肯錫諮詢公司預測，到2040年，非洲將擁有全世界最大規模的勞動力，工作年齡人扣將超11億人，但在非洲當前人口中，超過60%的人生活水平仍然低於每天2美元。

en: It is obvious that while many Africans have benefited from political emancipation – the legacy of Nyerere’s generation – poverty remains a significant obstacle.
zh: 顯然，儘管許多非洲人從政治解放中獲益 — — 這是尼雷爾這一代人留下的遺產 — — 但貧困仍然是一個巨大的障礙。

en: Unleashing the employment potential of African women is the best way to overcome it.
zh: 釋放非洲婦女的就業潛力，是克服這一障礙的最佳辦法。

en: As it stands, Africa’s women continue to be underrepresented in key industries and executive roles, owing to workplace discrimination and patriarchal expectations at home.
zh: 目前，非洲婦女在重要行業和管理崗位上仍然鮮有代表人物，造成這一現象的原因是職場歧視和父權家庭。

en: Unless barriers to entering the formal economy are removed and women are presented with options that enable them to realize their full potential, Africa’s socioeconomic development will continue to be impeded.
zh: 除非能夠取消阻礙婦女進入正式經濟的壁壘，讓婦女擁有充分實現她們的潛力的選擇，否則非洲社會經濟發展將繼續飽受抑制。

en: But while women are essential to the continent’s progress, they are still too often regarded as being secondary.
zh: 但是，儘管婦女對於非洲的進步至關重要，她們仍然常被視為二等公民。

en: Women must therefore claim their right to sit where decisions are made, and to shape the policies, plans, and strategies that will affect their lives and the lives of Africans for generations to come.
zh: 因此，婦女必須主張她們參與決策的權利，主張她們參與影響她們以及未來非洲人民生活的政策、計劃和戰略的權利。

en: Studies have shown that if more women had access to male-dominated occupations in Africa, worker productivity would rise by as much as 25%.
zh: 研究表明，如果更多的非洲婦女能夠獲得男性主宰的職位，勞動生產率將提高多達 25 % 。

en: That would be good for the overall economy, but also for women in general, as it would open up new avenues for social empowerment.
zh: 這對於總體經濟來說是一個好訊息，對一般婦女來說也是好訊息，因為這會開啟新的社會賦權之門。

en: When women participate in the job market and engage actively in business or political decision-making, patriarchal power dynamics shift, elevating the social status of women.
zh: 如果婦女能夠進入就業市場，積極參與商業或政治決策，父權社會的動態就會發生改變，提高婦女的社會地位。

en: Economic equality also challenges accepted beliefs, and dispels harmful myths that perpetuate narrow definitions of gender norms.
zh: 經濟平等也在挑戰現有的信念，消除讓狹隘的性別規範大行其道的有害的傳說。

en: In other words, bringing more women into the workplace leads to an emancipation of mindset – in men and women alike.
zh: 換句話說，讓更多婦女進入職場，能夠帶來解放思維 — — 不管是對男性還是對女性。

en: What Nyerere so eloquently said of Africa as a whole is no less true for its women: unity is the key to realizing our potential.
zh: 尼雷爾對於非洲的雄辯之辭，對於非洲婦女同樣成立：聯合是實現我們的潛力的關鍵。

en: When we come together as generators of wealth, it becomes impossible for us to go unrecognized for our economic contributions and marginalized in our entrepreneurial endeavours.
zh: 當我們擰成一股繩，成為財富的創造者，我們的經濟貢獻就不會得不到承認，我們在我們的創業努力中也不會被邊緣化。

en: At the Graça Machel Trust, we are joining together with civil-society actors, the private sector, and governments across the continent to lead a new economic liberation movement for women.
zh: 在格拉夏·馬謝爾信託，我們與全非洲的公民社會行動方、私人部門和政府合作，領導著一場婦女經濟解放運動。

en: Divided, we are weak, but together, Africa’s women have the ability to confront and overcome the barriers that have kept us from full participation in our respective economies.
zh: 分則弱，但如果我們能夠合在一起，非洲婦女就有能力面對和克服讓我們無法充分參與到各自經濟中的障礙。

en: There is power in networks.
zh: 網路存在力量。

en: My organization’s approach to economic advancement is to establish and strengthen informal and official networks, through which women can, in time, increase their participation and visibility in key sectors.
zh: 我的組織對於經濟進步的方針就是建立和強化非正式的和官方的網路，透過這些網路，婦女能夠及時提高她們在重要部門的參與度和辨識度（visibility ） 。

en: That is why we are launching the “Women Advancing Africa” initiative, which is part of our ongoing effort to amplify the voices of Africa’s underrepresented and to establish a pan-African women’s movement, in which women can come together to transform the continent.
zh: 因此，我們啟動了“婦女推動非洲 ” （ Women Advancing Africa）計劃，這是我們強化沒有贏得足夠代表的群體的聲音，以及建立一個讓婦女聯合起來改變非洲的泛非洲婦女運動的努力的一部分。

en: The inaugural Women Advancing Africa Forum will take place this week in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, and will convene more than 250 women leaders from across the continent.
zh: 婦女推動非洲論壇將於本週在坦尚尼亞達累斯薩拉姆正式起航，屆時將有來自非洲各地的250多位婦女領袖與會。

en: Under the overarching theme of “Driving Social and Economic Transformation,” the Forum will focus on three strategic goals: promoting financial inclusion, increasing market access, and driving social change.
zh: 論壇的總主題是“推動社會和經濟轉型 ” ， 將關注三個戰略性目標：促進金融包容、增加市場準入，一級推動社會變革。

en: We aim to emerge from the Forum with a common agenda for our participation as full economic actors.
zh: 我們的目標是透過論壇形成一個共同日程，讓我們成為全面的經濟參與者。

en: It has been just over 20 years since Nyerere encouraged us to work toward African unity.
zh: 尼雷爾鼓勵我們致力於非洲的聯合不過20年。

en: Today, Africa’s women are helping to shape the policies and practices that will bring about economic and social liberation in their respective countries.
zh: 如今，非洲婦女正在影響能給各自國家帶來經濟和社會解放的政策和實踐。

en: We have some way to go before African unity is fully realized.
zh: 充分實現非洲聯合還有很長的路要走。

en: But enabling women to become full partners in Africa’s economic future, is among the best ways to ensure that we succeed.
zh: 但讓婦女成為非洲經濟未來的全面夥伴，則是確保我們能夠成功的最佳辦法之一。

en: Capitalizing on Africa’s Youth Dividend
zh: 利用非洲的年輕人紅利

en: TORONTO – When South African university students took to the streets in 2016 as part of the “Fees Must Fall” protest movement, the “decolonization of the curriculum” was among the movement’s chief concerns.
zh: 多倫多—2016年，南非大學生紛紛走上街頭，這是“必須降學費”運動的一部分。 當時 ， “ 課程的去殖民地化”是這場運動的核心訴求之一。

en: It was a pivotal moment in South Africa’s history, as young people rose to demand quality and accessible education.
zh: 這場運動也是南非的一個歷史轉折點，年輕人開始站起來要求高品質的普及教育。

en: But a crucial question was missing from the debate over fees and curricular relevance: how can changes to higher education empower Africa’s youth to drive the continent’s economic transformation?
zh: 但這場關於學費和課程的爭論遺漏了一個關鍵問題：更高的教育程度如何讓非洲青年贏得力量，推動非洲經濟轉型？

en: For Africa, the question is no longer “if” students are taught, but “what.”
zh: 對非洲來說，學生受到教育已經不是“是否”的問題，而是學到“什麼”的問題。

en: Unfortunately, while access to education has improved significantly in recent decades, school curricula have changed little since the colonial era, when secondary education was an elite privilege designed to advance the careers of a select few.
zh: 不幸的是，儘管教育普及在近幾十年來有了重大改善，但學校課程並沒有較之殖民地時代有多少變化。 在殖民地時代，中等教育是一種精英特權，是專為一小撮人的職業生涯而設計的。

en: Technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programs have also suffered from neglect.
zh: 技術和在職教育和培訓（TVET）也因為不受重視而蒙受損失。

en: Today, these initiatives are marked by outdated courses and rote learning methods that fail to prepare young people for the demands of the twenty-first-century job market.
zh: 如今，這些專案課程陳舊，學習方法呆板，無法讓年輕人適應二十一世紀就業市場的需求。

en: The trouble goes beyond traditional components of the curriculum, like math, science, and language. There is also a deficiency in critical “soft” skills, such as communication, teamwork, and problem solving.
zh: 問題不僅在於課程的傳統內容，如數學、科學和語言上，也在於缺乏重要的“軟”技能，如溝通、團隊合作和解決問題。

en: Though neglected, it is these skills that enable young people to become adaptable, lifelong learners.
zh: 儘管這些技能不受重視，但它們能讓年輕人成為適應能力卓著的終身學習者。

en: The mastery of soft skills correlates to improved outcomes in school, work, and life.
zh: 掌握軟技能與學業、工作和生活結果的改善之間存在相關性。

en: Yet, until recently, training in soft skills has not been integrated into formal education systems on the continent.
zh: 但是，直到最近，軟技能的訓練仍然沒有納入非洲的正規教育體系中。

en: Fortunately, that is changing.
zh: 幸運的是，情況正在起變化。

en: Across the continent, secondary schools and TVET systems are transforming themselves to prepare Africa’s young minds with the skills they need to make the transition from school to employment, and to become more engaged citizens.
zh: 在整個非洲，中等學校和TVET系統正在實現轉型，準備好用完成學生到工作者和參與度更高的公民的轉變所必須的技能，來武裝非洲的年輕頭腦。

en: These adjustments are coming at a critical time for Africa, where many countries are experiencing a demographic dividend of declining fertility rates and rising productivity.
zh: 這些調整的到來正逢非洲的關鍵時刻。 許多非洲國家正在經歷生育率下降、生產率提高的人口紅利。

en: In particular, these changes mean more opportunity for young people as they prepare to enter the job market.
zh: 特別是，這些變化意味著年輕人在準備進入就業市場時可以獲得更多機會。

en: But to succeed on the job, young people must have the skills and education that a modern economy requires.
zh: 但要取得職場成功，年輕人必須具備現代經濟所要求的技能和教育。

en: At The MasterCard Foundation, where I manage education and learning programs, we’ve put together a blueprint – called Skills at Scale – to help African educators revitalize their curricula to capitalize more effectively on the economic potential of youth.
zh: 在萬事達卡基金會，我負責管理教育和學習專案。 我們制定了一個藍圖 — — 稱為《大規模技能 》 （ Skills at Scale ） — —以幫助非洲教育者透過課程設定更有效地發揮年輕人的經濟潛力。

en: One of the continent’s most successful efforts already underway is the USAID-funded Akazi Kanoze Youth Livelihoods Project, designed by the Education Development Center (EDC) in Boston.
zh: 目前，非洲正在實施的最成功的專案之一是美國國際開發署贊助的阿卡茲·卡諾澤年輕人生計計劃（Akazi Kanoze Youth Livelihoods Project ） ， 該計劃由波士頓的教育發展中心（Education Development Center ，EDC）制定。

en: Akazi Kanoze epitomizes how a small initiative can catalyze wider education-sector reform, by emphasizing links to local employers that provide access to entry-level jobs, internships, and apprenticeships.
zh: 阿卡茲·卡諾澤計劃充分說明了一個小規模的專案如何透過強調提供入門崗位、實習和學徒機會的本地僱主，帶來大規模的教育改革。

en: The focus on personal development, interpersonal communication, and leadership training has ensured that students are well equipped to enter the labor market upon graduation.
zh: 其注重個人發展、人際溝通和領導力培訓的做法確保了學生充分做好了一畢業就能進入勞動力市場的準備。

en: Rwanda’s Ministry of Education has already moved to integrate elements of the program in TVETs across the country.
zh: 盧安達教育部已經準備將該計劃的藥物納入到全國TVWT專案中。

en: The government recently integrated Akazi Kanoze’s approach in the national curriculum to equip secondary and TVET students with the soft skills they require to succeed.
zh: 盧安達政府最近在全國課程體系中納入了阿卡茲·卡諾澤計劃的方法，讓中等學校和TVET學生具備取得成功所需要的軟技能。

en: National exams in the 2018-2019 academic year will also reflect the new competency-based curriculum.
zh: 2018—2019學年國家統考也將體現新的基於能力的課程。

en: Since 2009, Akazi Kanoze trainings have prepared more than 37,000 youth for work, with more than 65% of participants in the initial round of training employed six months after graduation.
zh: 2009年以來，阿卡茲·卡諾澤計劃培訓了37,000多位年輕人，其中65%的首輪培訓參與者在畢業後六個月內找到了工作。

en: Based on the success of integrating soft skills into the curriculum in Rwanda, The MasterCard Foundation and EDC will launch a similar program in Senegal later this year.
zh: 基於在盧安達取得了將軟技能納入課程的成功，萬事達卡基金會和EDC將在今年晚些時候在塞內加爾啟動一項類似的計劃。

en: Case studies from Skills at Scale highlight six components to a successful skills-training initiative.
zh: 來自《大規模技能》的案例研究強調了成功的技能培訓計劃的六個要素。

en: These include an enabling policy environment, in which the government is supportive and sets clear goals for education sector reform; vocal backing for these changes from strong political champions; wide stakeholder engagement, especially in the design and implementation phases of the reform; decentralization of authority for education; flexibility on the part of donors; and the ability to measure the changes’ impact on youth employment and entrepreneurship.
zh: 它們包括有利的政策環境（政府持支援臺獨，併為教育部門改革制定明確的目標 ） 、 政治要人對這些改變的口頭支援、相關利益方的廣泛參與（特別是在改革的設計和實施階段 ） 、 教育權力的分散化、出資者的靈活性，以及衡量改變對年輕人就業和企業家精神的影響的能力。

en: Change is not without challenge.
zh: 改變不是沒有挑戰的。

en: Adapting models of skills training to vastly different education systems across Africa will take time.
zh: 調整技能培訓模式依適應非洲多變的教育體系需要時間。

en: It will also be difficult to ensure that intensive training models reach all young people, including those no longer in school.
zh: 確保密集培訓模式觸及所有年輕人，包括早已不在上學的人也將十分困難。

en: Experience in Rwanda shows that curriculum redesign requires close cooperation with education and workforce development authorities, as well as government officials, teachers, and school administrators.
zh: 盧安達的經驗表明，課程的重新設計需要與教育和勞工發展當局的緊密合作，政府官員、教師和學校管理者也要參與其中。

en: New curriculum content also requires developing new teaching and learning materials.
zh: 新的課程內容還要求開發新的教學和學習材料。

en: Achieving scale also requires a markedly different approach to training teachers than is currently on offer in most African school systems.
zh: 實現規模還需要採取與大部分非洲學校體系現行做法截然不同的方法去培訓老師。

en: Trainings must go beyond traditional, one-off approaches, by providing ongoing teacher support.
zh: 培訓必須超越傳統的一次性方法，而要持續提供教師支援。

en: New pedagogies also require continual supervision and practice, especially early on.
zh: 新的教學法還需要洲級監督和實踐，特別是在早期。

en: The old “cascade” model of teacher training simply won’t work.
zh: 舊的教師培訓“階梯 ” （ cascade）模式已經完全失去了效果。

en: African governments, with support from the international community, can help students’ transition from school to work by relying on a curriculum that elevates the importance of soft skills.
zh: 在國際社會的幫助下，非洲政府可以透過強調軟技能的重要性的課程，幫助學生從校園到工作崗位的轉型。

en: If done well, these changes can ensure young people are positioned to drive Africa’s future prosperity.
zh: 如果順利的話，這些變化能夠確保年輕人推動非洲的未來繁榮。

en: Africans deserve a forward-looking education system, not one that remains stuck in the past.
zh: 非洲人民理應獲得具有前瞻性，而不是陷在過去難以自拔的教育體系。

en: As students in South Africa demonstrated last year, the continent’s youth will settle for nothing less.
zh: 南非學生在去年已經證明，只有這樣才能令非洲年輕人滿足。

en: A Big Bond for Africa
zh: 非洲大債券

en: LAGOS – The countries of Sub-Saharan Africa have reached a critical juncture.
zh: 拉各斯—撒哈拉以南非洲諸國走到了關鍵時刻。

en: Strained by a collapse in commodity prices and China’s economic slowdown, the region’s growth slipped to 3.4% in 2015 – nearly 50% lower than the average rate over the previous 15 years.
zh: 受困於大宗商品價格暴跌和中國經濟減速，2015年該地區增長率下滑到3.4 % — —比此前15年的平均水平低了近50 % 。

en: The estimated growth rate for 2016 is lower than the population growth rate of about 2%, implying a per capita contraction in GDP.
zh: 2016年預計增長率更是低於2%左右的人口增長率，這意味著人均GDP將有所下降。

en: Sustained economic growth is essential to maintain progress on reducing poverty, infant mortality, disease, and malnutrition.
zh: 持續的經濟增長對於保持降低貧困、嬰兒死亡率、疾病和營養不良等方面的進步至關重要。

en: It is also the only way to create sufficient good jobs for Africa’s burgeoning youth population – the fastest growing in the world.
zh: 保持經濟增長也是為不斷膨脹的年輕人口創造足夠的優質崗位的唯一辦法 — — 非洲年輕人口增長率為世界之最。

en: As Gerd Müller, Germany’s development minister, noted at a recent press conference, “If the youth of Africa can’t find work or a future in their own countries, it won’t be hundreds of thousands, but millions that make their way to Europe.”
zh: 德國發展部長戈爾德·穆勒（Gerd Müller）在最近的新聞釋出會上指出 ， “ 如果非洲年輕人不能在祖國找到工作和未來，就會有數百萬計，而不是幾萬或幾十萬人想方設法來到歐洲。 ”

en: One way to sustain growth and create jobs would be to collaborate on planning and implementing a massive increase in infrastructure investment across Africa.
zh: 保持增長、創造就業的一個辦法是在整個非洲共同規劃和實施大規模增加基礎設施投資。

en: Public infrastructure is particularly important.
zh: 公共基礎設施尤其重要。

en: This includes highways, bridges, and railways linking rural producers in landlocked countries to Africa’s urban consumers and external markets; mass transit and Internet infrastructure to accommodate greater commercial activity; and electricity transmission lines integrating privately financed power plants and grids.
zh: 它們包括高速公路、橋樑和鐵路，將內陸國的農業生產者與非洲城市消費者和外部市場連線起來；包括大規模運輸和網際網路基礎設施，以容納更多的商業活動；也包括輸電線路，將私人融資的發電廠和電網融合在一起。

en: Major regional projects are also needed to knit together Sub-Saharan Africa’s many tiny economies.
zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲的許多微型經濟體也需要透過大型地區專案聯絡在一起。

en: This is the only way to create the economies of scale needed to increase the export potential of African agriculture and industry, as well as to reduce domestic prices of food and manufactured goods.
zh: 這是創造規模經濟的唯一辦法，而國模經濟則是提升非洲農業和工業出口潛力，以及降低食品和製造品的國內價格的必要條件。

en: While governments in Africa are spending more on public infrastructure themselves, outside finance is still required, especially for regional projects, which are rarely a top priority for national governments.
zh: 儘管非洲各國政府正在增加自身的公共基礎設施支出，但仍然需要外部融資，特別是對於很少成為國家政府重中之重的地區專案。

en: Yet aid from Africa’s traditionally generous foreign donors, including the United States and Europe, is now set to shrink, owing to political and economic constraints.
zh: 但傳統的慷慨出資者，包括美國和歐洲，目前都因為政治和經濟約束而準備縮減援助。

en: But there may be a solution that helps Africa recover its growth in a way that Western leaders and their constituents find acceptable.
zh: 但也許存在一種辦法，可以幫助非洲增長恢復，並且被西方領導人和他們的選民所接受。

en: We call it the “Big Bond” – a strategy for leveraging foreign aid funds in international capital markets to generate financing for massive infrastructure investment.
zh: 我們稱之為“大債券 ” — —利用外國援助資金作為國際資本市場槓桿，為大規模基礎設施投資籌集融資。

en: Specifically, donors would borrow against future aid flows in capital markets.
zh: 具體而言，出資者可以在資本市場中，根據未來援助流貸款。

en: That way, they could exploit current low interest rates at home, as they generate new resources.
zh: 如此，它們可以利用目前本國的低利率來開源。

en: With 30-year US Treasury rates of about 3%, donors would have to securitize only about $5 billion to raise $100 billion.
zh: 30年美國國債利率大約在3 % ， 出資者只需要證券化大約50億美元，就能籌集1,000億美元。

en: That money could come from the $35 billion in annual official development assistance (ODA) to Africa (which totals about $50 billion) that takes the form of pure grants.
zh: 這筆錢可以來自每年對非洲的純捐贈形式的350億官方發展援助（ODA，總量大約為500億美元 ） 。

en: Donors would pass on the interest cost to African countries, reducing their own fiscal costs.
zh: 出資者可以將利息成本磚家給非洲國家，降低它們自身的財政負擔。

en: For African countries, the terms would be better than those provided by Eurobonds.
zh: 對非洲國家來說，條件也要優於歐元債券所提供的條件。

en: In fact, as audacious as it may sound, passing on the interest costs to recipient countries could actually bolster their debt sustainability.
zh: 事實上，儘管這聽上去有些冒險，將利息成本轉嫁給受資國實際上可以加強它們的債務可持續性。

en: According to a study of eight countries by the African Development Bank’s Policy Innovation Lab, a 3% interest rate in US dollar terms would be lower than the marginal cost of commercial borrowings undertaken by several African countries over the last five years.
zh: 據非洲開發銀行政策創新實驗室（Policy Innovation Lab）的一項針對八個國家的研究，3%的美元利率將比一些非洲國家在過去五年中進行的商業借貸的邊際成本更低。

en: Moreover, far longer maturities and grace periods, compared to market finance, would ease growing pressure on foreign-exchange reserves.
zh: 此外，與市場融資相比遠遠更長的期限和寬限期將緩解對外匯儲備的壓力。

en: Frontloading aid in this way is not new.
zh: 這種形式的前置援助並非新事物。

en: Doing so in the early 2000s to finance vaccines saved millions of lives in the developing world.
zh: 21世紀初，以這種方式進行的疫苗融資拯救了數百萬發展中國家的生命。

en: Big Bond resources, managed by the African Development Bank, could be used to help guarantee financing for major regional infrastructure projects that have long been stuck on the back burner, such as the East Africa Railway connecting Tanzania, Rwanda, and Burundi, and a highway stretching from Nigeria to Côte d’Ivoire.
zh: 在非洲開發銀行的管理下，大債券資源可用於保證長期無法得到重點照顧的大型地區基礎設施專案的融資，如連線坦尚尼亞、盧安達和蒲隆地的東非鐵路以及從奈及利亞通往象牙海岸的高速公路。

en: Such projects could also be co-financed by private investors.
zh: 這些專案也可以與私人投資者合作共同融資。

en: Moreover, the Big Bond could help to reinvigorate the relationship between donors and African countries.
zh: 此外，大債券有助於重振出資者和非洲國家之間的關係。

en: And, as it supports investments with important country-level benefits, it could serve as an incentive for African countries to pursue reforms that increase their absorptive capacity, in terms of choosing and executing public infrastructure investments.
zh: 此外，由於它支援能帶來重要的國家層面收益的投資，因此可以成為非洲國家實施改革的激勵，提高它們的吸收能力 — — 如選擇和執行公共基礎設施投資。
